name: Sylvae
tagline: Grow useful work. Keep a receipt for every run.
description: Sylvae carries a small, portable skill to the worker you choose—local or hosted—and records what happened. It helps a team spend attention and computation where they are actually needed.
status: Active development · portable runner and local review surface
motifCaption: The grove: shared knowledge, different workers, visible roots.

links.label: Read The Loom and the Grove

highlights.label: Portable knowledge
highlights.title: The skill is not the vendor
highlights.text: Keep instructions in SKILL.md. The same know-how can travel between local models, hosted APIs and agent harnesses.

highlights.label: Honest outcomes
highlights.title: A receipt, not a promise
highlights.text: Each run has an identity and durable record. A backend that could not run is unavailable, not a failed answer.

highlights.label: Economical care
highlights.title: Choose the appropriate worker
highlights.text: Use an explicit backend or declared tier. Avoid paying full agent overhead for work that a small, local model can do well.

sections.title: Knowledge should grow roots, not vendor lock-in.
paragraphs: Sylvae is RAGBAZ’s portable skill runner. It loads a SKILL.md-format instruction and runs it through Ollama, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or the Anthropic API. Four backends reuse existing CLI tools and their configured accounts.

Skills can express cheap, frontier or agent tiers. Automatic routing is configurable; an unspecified tier is not assumed cheap. Explicit choices are important because real agent runs carry real latency, token use and cost.
A team can accumulate useful practices—summarising a change, checking a report or explaining disk use—without tying every instruction to one provider.

sections.title: Spend the frontier effort where it earns its place.
paragraphs: A measured trivial Claude Code prompt in the project documentation used 28,424 tokens and $0.171 with default settings, compared with 3,146 tokens and $0.027 after trimming unused setup. That example illustrates overhead; it is not a universal savings guarantee.

Local inference can offer control and avoid an API fee, but hardware, electricity and maintenance are still costs. A capable small worker is useful only when its output is good enough for the task and somebody can check that.
This is part of the studio’s wider ethic: reduce needless consumption, make constraints visible, and preserve people’s freedom to choose the tools that fit their circumstances.

sections.title: Make a run understandable after the conversation is gone.
paragraphs: A run record preserves skill, backend, model, timing and outcome. The local review page can browse records and deliberately trigger another run. It is not an inexpensive pretend preview: those backends perform real work.
A coordinator may preallocate a run ID and use it as WeftMark’s evidence producer identity. Sylvae keeps the run receipt; WeftMark keeps the commit-bound engineering evidence.
Nostoi can verify the separate audit chain. Reading a page is not a review decision, and a cryptographic signature does not prove the skill’s answer was correct.

links.label: Verify the audit trail with Nostoi

sections.title: A cooperative tool, not a replacement for responsibility.
paragraphs: We want people to be able to experiment without being pressured into blind trust or an expensive subscription. Explicit routing, accessible run records and portable instructions are practical ways to support mutual cooperation.

Concerns about AI misuse, unpredictable behaviour or people using AI to harm others deserve serious attention. Sylvae records execution and helps organise bounded work; it does not itself guarantee that an agent is harmless or that a generated result is true.
In Rebekah, the runner sits within a reproducible, authenticated runtime. Human review and, when explicitly enabled, Ephor governance add different kinds of oversight.

workflow.title: Write one useful skill
workflow.text: Describe the job and expected output in SKILL.md. Start small enough that another person can understand and assess the result.

workflow.title: Choose a backend deliberately
workflow.text: Use an explicit local model for a first experiment, or configure the tier mapping for your actual host and accounts.

workflow.title: Read the receipt
workflow.text: Inspect the run’s input, output, model and status. Treat unavailable, failed and successful runs as different observations.

workflow.title: Bring the result into review
workflow.text: Correlate the run ID with WeftMark evidence, verify audit integrity with Nostoi where useful, and leave the human judgment explicit.
workflow.linkLabel: Bring the threads to the loom

quickstart.title: Run one local skill
quickstart.summary: Use a source checkout, Python environment and an already configured Ollama installation. Download the model you intend to use and prepare a small input file.
quickstart.note: Model downloads need storage and bandwidth. Hosted and agent backends have their own credentials and costs; do not assume automatic routing is free.

commands.label: Install
commands.code:
git clone https://github.com/tabenius/sylvae.git
cd sylvae
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install .

commands.label: Choose a model and run a skill
commands.code:
ollama pull mistral:latest
sylvae run skills/summarize-diff --backend ollama \
  --model mistral:latest --input /path/to/a/diff.txt

pages.title: From a skill to a useful receipt
pages.description: A practical path from an explicit backend choice to a run record and commit-bound evidence.

sections.title: Start small and explicit
paragraphs: Pick a skill and a small input whose quality you can assess. Name the backend and model rather than relying on someone else’s host defaults.
Read the recorded outcome. A missing backend, unavailable budget or denied invocation is not the same as a skill that ran and produced an unsuccessful result.

sections.title: Make correlation deliberate
paragraphs: A coordinator can preallocate Sylvae’s canonical 32-character lowercase run ID and use sylvae:run/<id> as WeftMark’s evidence producer. Execute the real skill command through WeftMark when you need commit-bound evidence.
Keep the run receipt, engineering evidence and audit chain distinct. They complement each other; none can silently grant approval on behalf of a person.

sections.title: Finish with a human question
paragraphs: Does the result serve the purpose? What was not checked? Who can continue the work? Those questions connect the economical runner to a considerate, accountable workflow.
